title: Lightweight session-proxy patterns for tool calls in SDKs (TS/Py/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a small, language-idiomatic session-proxy pattern across TypeScript/Python/Go SDKs that standardizes streaming + tool/function-calling lifecycles and produces validated structured outputs.\n\nContext: Multiple teams are implementing streaming tool calls with slightly different session semantics: event envelopes, reentrancy, resume tokens, and structured result validation. This causes incompatibilities for cross-service integrations and increases maintenance. We want a minimal shim that SDKs can expose to app devs that: 1) normalizes streaming frames into language-native async iterators/callbacks, 2) surfaces tool invocation lifecycle (invoke, progress, result, error, fallback) consistently, 3) includes a small typed validator hook for structured outputs (JSON Schema / pydantic / go structs), and 4) provides a compatibility adapter to bridge legacy callback-based clients.
non_goals: Replacing user application frameworks (we provide patterns, not full orchestration)
Implementing heavy-weight session brokers or persistent proxy services (out of scope)
Full eval harnesses or QA for every downstream consumer (we'll provide integration tests and examples)
Language bindings beyond TS/Py/Go in this wave
acceptance_criteria: TS/Py/Go SDKs expose a SessionProxy abstraction with consistent lifecycle events (invoke, progress, output, done, error)
Sample app in each language demonstrates: streaming tool call -> progress frames -> structured output validated against a schema -> graceful resume after transient disconnect
Compatibility adapter that accepts legacy callback-style handlers and emits the new SessionProxy events (examples in README)
Automated unit tests covering resume token logic and KV cache hint propagation
Engineering docs and examples landed in SDK repo and linked from developer docs (sdk-2025.03)
Performance regression < 5% p50 for fast-path non-streaming calls when proxy is present

decisions: Use a small JSON event envelope with 'type' and 'payload' keys; avoid heavy framing protocols to keep bandwidth low
Expose async iterators in TS/Py and channels in Go as the primary streaming primitive for ergonomics
Structured output validation will be opt-in via a validator hook to avoid runtime cost for callers that don't need it
Compatibility adapter will be implemented in-language and distributed as a thin helper rather than as a separate service
Resume tokens will be opaque strings issued by the runtime; SDKs should cache the last committed token and include it on reconnect attempts
